name: AMoRE
summary: AMoRE searches for neutrinoless double-beta decay of molybdenum-100 with scintillating crystals at millikelvin temperatures. Its pilot and AMoRE-I stages at Yangyang established the method for the larger AMoRE-II programme at Yemilab.
detection_principle: A molybdate crystal absorbs the decay energy. Metallic magnetic calorimeters measure heat and scintillation simultaneously; their ratio separates alpha backgrounds from electron events near the double-beta endpoint.

status.label: Completed pilot and AMoRE-I / AMoRE-II construction
status.evidence: AMoRE-I completed its two-year dataset and published its final search in 2025. The August 2025 collaboration report describes AMoRE-II detector construction and commissioning of its housing at Yemilab; completion of the first stage later in 2025 was a schedule, not an established milestone.

phases.name: AMoRE-Pilot / AMoRE-I
phases.description: Predecessor molybdate-calorimeter stages at Yangyang established the detection method and published rare-decay constraints.

phases.name: AMoRE-II
phases.description: Lithium-molybdate array under staged construction at Yemilab in the August 2025 collaboration report. Its housing was undergoing commissioning; forecast construction dates and sensitivity are not achieved measurements.

results.summary: The AMoRE-I final analysis found no neutrinoless double-beta decay of 100Mo and set T1/2 above 2.9 x 10^24 yr at 90% confidence from 3.89 kg yr of isotope exposure.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
